description: The team of warriors of code and life
summary:
Project Summary: A.R.I.S. (Advanced Responsive Integrated Suit Intelligence)

What we created:

A.R.I.S. is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring system and intelligent smart spacesuit. This system uses multi-modal biosensors to monitor cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and behavioural data. The system also has anomaly detection algorithms operating in real time, self-assessment tools and active emergency protocols.

How we solved the problem:

When exploring deep space, there will be a lag in communication between the astronaut and Earth. With A.R.I.S. the crew can monitor their health in real time with automatic risk detection and protocols for medical interventions.

Why it is important:

By allowing the astronaut to have an autonomous health triage system with continuous biosensors it can ensure they are still able to carry out vital operations whilst also keeping them safe and ensuring mission success.
details:
1. What does our Project Do? & How Does It Work?

This project is an interactive Jarvis Inspired Smart Spacesuit and Astronaut Health Monitoring System. The project acts as an intelligent interface with real time data from the suit, life support and the command system.

How it works:

Live Health and Suit Monitoring: This project takes live vital signs from the astronaut such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature and stress/fatigue levels. It also takes live data from the suit including oxygen tank level, suit pressure, CO₂ scrubber, battery life and radiation.

3D Interactive Visual: The main screen of this system has a 3D animated version of the smart spacesuit. It will show you interactive visuals depending on what the data is showing and what parts you interact with (Helmet HUD, Life Support Pack, Heating System).

AI Voice Assistant: This project uses English as the universal language which means it acts like an AI assistant. You can ask questions about your suit and run diagnostics with simple voice commands.

Automatic Emergency Response: If any of the data goes outside of the safety range, the project will automatically display and play an emergency alarm. It will isolate the issue, calculate remaining EVA time and send the most important data to the main ship.

2. What benefits does it provide?

Zero Latency Understanding: This project takes all data from dozens of sensors and puts them all together, reducing the astronauts cognitive workload.

Voice Commands: The astronauts can use voice commands to see what their vitals are, control heating and log issues whilst their hands are busy.

Early Detection: This project will automatically detect if any data goes out of range. This means any issues can be picked up early such as O2 leakage or increased heart rates.

Send Data To Mission Specialists: This project will automatically send all of the data to the mission specialists.

Expandable: since it uses generative AI, it can easily add modules, missions and diagnostics.

3. What impact will your project have?

With humans going further into space, we are now doing longer missions to the moon, mars and deep space. Communication with earth can take several minutes to over 20 minutes each way meaning we will not be able to have real time control from the ground.

This project will give astronauts an autonomous intelligence inside their suit that acts like a personal mission specialist. With real time health data, 3D visuals and voice AI it will:

Save lives in critical situations during EVA.

Increase mission time by not letting the astronauts get fatigued or have issues with life support.

Create inspiration for aerospace engineering by showing how the latest generative AI and web technology can create cutting edge human machine interfaces. This can also be used in high risk environments on earth such as deep sea divers, firefighters and hazardous material response.

4. What tools, languages and hardware did we use?

Our team created a unique multi AI solution using the latest LLM coding tools and generative video tools.

Google AI Studio: Was used to create the base of the application, logic, prompts and simulation.

Claude Code: Was used to improve the base, improve the UI and add the interactive 3D animation.

Google Gemini: Was used to come up with ideas for the project, create a structure for prompts to create visuals and code, debug and create code.

ChatGPT Image Generator: Was used to create detailed concept art, futuristic suit designs and base images.

Google AI Vids: Was used to create movement from the suit concepts and prompts.

Ezgif Video to JPG: Was used to create a series of high quality JPG images from the videos.

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript / TypeScript & React: Was used to create the UI, live vitals, frame sequence animations and styling for the HUD.

5. How is our project creative?

Frame Sequence 3D Animation: Rather than using resource heavy 3D modelling software we used our creativity to create a new way to create 3D animation. We used ChatGPT to create visuals, Google AI Vids to animate, Ezgif to create frame sequences and Claude Code to make them interactive. This creates rich cinematic 3D visuals.

Multiple AIs: We gave each AI its own role. Gemini was the creative director and prompt designer. Google AI Studio was the main engine. Chat GPT and Google AI Vids was the visual effects team and Claude Code was the main programmer.

JARVIS Style: Most dashboards are just massive spreadsheets of data. This project converts the complex data into a simple Sci-Fi style HUD with voice. This makes it easy to understand any important information.

6. What did you consider?

Human Factors: In an emergency the astronaut won’t have time to read lots of text. We made sure all of the data was shown using high contrast visuals, colours to indicate issues and short voice alerts.

Performance: Using high quality 3D visuals can cause crashes in regular browsers. We converted the animations into frame sequences with Ezgif to make sure we had smooth transitions on regular laptops.

Realistic: When creating the data we considered realistic factors when astronauts would be in space. For example increased exercise will increase heart rates and O2 usage whilst increasing CO₂.

No Internet: Deep space suits will not have internet. We made sure the suit would work with no internet by creating local state and instant alerts.

Visual Consistency: We made sure the AI generated visuals would match the color scheme, font and design of the HUD. This makes the 3D suit look like it would fit in with the rest of the dashboard.

So, these are all the specifications and properties of our project A.R.I.S (Health monitoring software for astronauts in space missions).
